$description: BUILDER INPUT for REVIEW-principles-into-graph-2026-09-15-v1.html (#275 lane RP). Every {placeholder} below is filled at build time from notes/_lanes/275/principles-kg/dry-run.json or from a live measurement in _build_page.py — no integer is typed into this file or into the HTML. ⚠ The review page EXPORTS Dave's answers under this same filename (the RK convention: {page, at, decisions:[{id, choice, note}]}). If that export is ever copied over this file, _build_page.py REFUSES with a named error instead of building a page with no copy on it.
title: Principles into the graph — #275 decision page
headline: The register has 145 rows. The graph has none of them.

decisions.title: The node, and what it carries
decisions.lede: A register row becomes one node: ux:<id>, e.g. ux:pr-fitts. {principles} nodes. The prefix is not in question — s269-D2 ruled it, and this lane re-measured it free: the live graph carries {live_prefixes} prefixes and ux: is not one of them, while principle: and guideline: are WCAG's. What is open is the payload.
options: a

All twelve register fields, verbatim — statement, family, originator, year, grade, grade_alt, grade_reason, evidence, scope_conditions, known_misreadings, refutation_probe — plus gradeName, read from the s237-D1 map rather than retyped. About {payload_full_kb} KB.
b
The head only: id, statement, family, grade, originator, year (about {payload_trim_kb} KB). The four long prose fields stay in principles.json and the graph points at the file.
c
Hold. The {principles} stay out of the graph and keep living in knowledge/brain/principles.json alone.
decisions.why: Why (a): the register exists because a principle read without its scope conditions is a principle misread — Fitts taken as ‘make buttons big’ is the register's own example. A node that carries the statement and drops the misreadings reproduces the problem. The cost is {payload_full_kb} KB against an explorer page that is already {explorer_mb} MB.

decisions.title: Which edge types land in wave 1
decisions.lede: Six edge types are measured: {edges} edges across {nodes} nodes. Nothing is invented — an unresolvable target is null plus the evidence, and there are {unresolved} of those.
options: a
All six: tensionWith {tensionWith} · hasParty {hasParty} · touches {touches} · resolvedBy {resolvedBy} · challengedBy {challengedBy} · explainedBy {explainedBy}.
b
tensionWith only ({tensionWith}) — the principles and the tensions between them, nothing else. This is RP-3 (b) in edge form.
c
All six, but the four typed links collapsed into one polarityLink edge carrying a linkType attribute — three new words in the vocabulary instead of six.
d
All six plus inFamily ({inFamily_edges} edges to {family_hubs} hubs) and evidencedBy ({evidence_edges} edges to {evidence_nodes} new evidence: nodes): {all_eight} edges.
decisions.why: Why (a): every one of the {edges} is read from a field or from a generated file with a declared derivation rule. Nothing is parsed out of prose, which is what made cites the weak one at #274. (c) saves three words but spends s238-D6, which ruled the link typed precisely so that the type carries the claim. (d)'s evidencedBy is the one type that already exists — and 0 of its {evidence_nodes} URLs join a live evidence: node, so the word would come to mean a chat receipt in one family and a journal citation in another.

decisions.title: The polarity: a node, or only an attribute on an edge
decisions.lede: {polarities} polarities. {polarity_edges} of them already derive a pairwise edge into _generated/polarity-edges.json, and this lane re-derived all {tensionWith} from polarities.json and got the same set — the view is fresh, proved, not assumed. The either/or the #269 inventory left open is whether the polarity itself is a node.
options: a

polarity:<id> — {polarities} nodes. The home for the {edgeless} polarities that derive no pair at all, the {links} typed citations to rulings, and the {not_edgeable} parties that are a declared stub or a ruling rather than a register row.
b

No node. The {tensionWith} tensionWith edges only, with the polarity id and its mediating variable carried as edge attributes. Measured cost: {edgeless} polarities and {links} typed links leave no trace — {unresolved_nopn} declared losses against {unresolved}.
c
A node only for the {polarity_edges} that derive a pair; the {edgeless} edgeless ones stay out.
decisions.why: Why (a): s238-D1 already ruled the shape — the polarity's home is a node with N typed parties that must resolve and typed out-links, and the pairwise edges are derived, never authored. This is that model, in the graph. It also passes the s274-D9 test rather than dodging it: a hub that carries nothing earns no edge, and this one carries a mediating-variable sentence, a derived status, {links} typed citations and {not_edgeable} parties no pair edge can express.

decisions.title: The 20 principles that restate a standard we already hold
decisions.lede: {wcag} rows sit in standards families — fam-wcag22 {fam_wcag22}, fam-coga {fam_coga}, fam-aria-apg {fam_aria}, fam-en301549 {fam_en}, fam-eaa {fam_eaa} — and the graph already holds those standards as {live_principle} principle:, {live_sc} sc:, {live_guideline} guideline:, a standard: and a policy: node. Measured across all twelve fields: 0 rows name any of them. {wcag_named} ids do contain a WCAG principle's name — and that is a name match.
options: a
Land the {wcag} as plain ux: nodes with no cross-link, and author the joins later in a named lane.
b
Author the {wcag_named} certain joins now, by hand, in a small authored file — and leave the other {wcag_rest}.
c
Hold the {wcag} out of the graph until the joins exist, so no row appears twice under two vocabularies.
decisions.why: Why (a): a join drawn by matching the word ‘perceivable’ is the thing s274-D12 refused yesterday for 27 rule → component candidates, and the reason was good. (b) is defensible for the four, and is the honest follow-up in the shape RK-4 took — a first, then c.

decisions.title: Component metas citing the six laws: which lane, and when
decisions.lede: s269-D5 says a component's meta cites the principles it rests on, starting with the six A-grade laws. Measured: 0 of {metas} metas names a pr- id, and 0 names any of the six laws verbatim. So this is authored work end to end, not a generator's. P-274-3 already parks the identical shape for rules (s274-D12's second half).
options: a
One lane, after this proposal lands, doing both at once: a handful of components cite the rules they obey (P-274-3) and the laws they rest on (s269-D5). One meta.schema.json diff, one review.
b
A principles-only lane now; the rules half waits for its own session.
c
Park it with a tripwire and decide when the CX principles arrive.
decisions.why: Why (a): the two are the same edit to the same file — a component meta gaining a citation array. Splitting them costs two schema diffs and two reviews for one change. Which components go first is yours; P-274-3 already records that.

decisions.title: Where the nodes live, and who reads them
decisions.lede: --land writes one new file, knowledge/_ux_principle_nodes.json, in the shape of _rule_nodes.json. Measured at run time, not asserted: _build_kg_explorer.py names _rule_nodes.json and does not name _ux_principle_nodes.json.
options: a
Land the file and teach _build_kg_explorer.py to read it in the same commit, behind its own chip. The s274-D11 precedent: section C of the explorer is the template.
b
File first, reader next session. The file sits inert until then.
c
No file: build the nodes inside _build_kg_explorer.py at build time, the way the WCAG family is built today.
decisions.why: Why (a): #274 asked this exact question and the answer held — the rules chip is live in explorer v1.11 and reads a landed file. A landed file no builder names is an instrument without a consumer, which is the failure your RK-5 note put your finger on.
